entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-01-.question: In Genesis 1:4, God separated the light from the waters.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-01-.learningObjective: Observe what God separates on the first day.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-01-.feedbackCorrect: God separated the light from the darkness; the waters are separated only later, in Genesis 1:6.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread the end of Genesis 1:4: God separated the light from the darkness.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-01-.hint: Look at the end of the verse.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-01-.question: In Genesis 1:4, tap what God saw was good.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-01-.learningObjective: Identify what God approves at the beginning of the story.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-01-.feedbackCorrect: The first thing the Bible calls good is the light God made.

feedbackWrong.a: "Separou" is something God does, not what he saw.
feedbackWrong.b: The darkness is separated from the light; the text does not say it was good.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-01-.hint: Look for what comes right before "era boa".

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-01-.question: According to Genesis 1:3, how does light come into being?
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-01-.learningObjective: Observe that light comes from God's word.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-01-.feedbackCorrect: God says "Que haja luz", and light exists: his word is enough.

feedbackWrong.a: Light does not spring from the darkness; it comes from God's word.
feedbackWrong.b: The Spirit was hovering over the waters (Gen 1:2); light comes when God speaks.
feedbackWrong.d: The text has not mentioned the sun yet; light comes from God's word.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-01-.hint: Read the beginning of the verse.

options.a: It appears on its own out of the darkness
options.b: The Spirit kindles it over the waters
options.d: It comes from the sun, which already existed

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-01-.question: Put Genesis 1:5 together in the order of the text.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-01-.feedbackCorrect: That is the verse's order: God names the light and the darkness, and then the first day is counted.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the names God gives; the first day closes the verse.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-01-.hint: The verse begins with God giving names.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-01-.question: In Genesis 1:2, what was the darkness over?
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-01-.learningObjective: Remember the setting before the light.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-01-.feedbackCorrect: Darkness over the deep: the dark, deep setting where the story will begin to take shape.

feedbackWrong.a: The text does not speak of dry land here; it speaks of a deep covered in darkness.
feedbackWrong.b: There are no mountains yet; the earth was formless and empty.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-01-.hint: Think of something deep and dark, linked to the waters.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-01-.question: What does Genesis 1:1 say that connects to this context?
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-01-.learningObjective: Connect Genesis 1:1 to the beginning of the whole biblical story.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-01-.feedbackCorrect: The first sentence of the whole Bible has God as its subject: the story begins with him.

feedbackWrong.b: Israel comes in much later, with Abraham; before any people, there is God.
feedbackWrong.c: Human beings come in later; the first sentence speaks of God creating.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-01-.hint: See who the subject of the first sentence is.

options.a: The whole story begins with God
options.c: The Bible begins with human beings

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-01-.question: In Genesis 1:3, light comes into being as a direct result of God's word.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-01-.learningObjective: Understand God's word as the cause of the light.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-01-.feedbackCorrect: God says "Que haja luz", and then comes "e houve luz": the word brings about what it says.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread Genesis 1:3: God speaks, and then "houve luz". There is no other cause.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-01-.hint: See what comes right after what God said.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-01-.question: In Genesis 1:5, tap the word that shows God's work is only beginning.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-01-.learningObjective: Recognize the sequence marker in the text.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-01-.feedbackCorrect: "Primeiro" starts a count: if there is a first day, the story will go on.

feedbackWrong.a: "Chamou" shows God giving names, not a sequence.
feedbackWrong.c: "Noite" is the name given to the darkness; it does not show that something will go on.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-01-.hint: Look for a word that starts a count.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-01-.question: In Genesis 1:4–5, what does God do after creating the light?
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-01-.learningObjective: Relate the creation of light to the order God establishes.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-01-.feedbackCorrect: God sees the light is good, separates light and darkness, and names each one: he brings order.

feedbackWrong.a: The darkness remains and receives a name: Night. God puts it in order.
feedbackWrong.b: Here the one who gives the names is God; human beings have not been created yet.
feedbackWrong.d: The text says God separated the light from the darkness.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-01-.hint: Follow the verbs: saw, separated, called.

options.a: He does away with the darkness forever
options.b: He asks human beings to give the names
options.c: He approves the light, separates, and names each part
options.d: He leaves light and darkness mixed together

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-01-.question: How does the scene move from Genesis 1:2 to 1:5?
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-01-.learningObjective: Understand the movement from emptiness to order.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-01-.feedbackCorrect: From dark emptiness to light through the word, then order: God approves, separates, and names.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the empty world; light comes through the word, and only then God separates and names.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-01-.hint: The starting point is the dark.

options.a: A world still empty and dark

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-01-.question: In Genesis 1:4, what does God do with the light and the darkness?
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-01-.learningObjective: Remember the action of God that brings order.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-01-.feedbackCorrect: To separate is to put each thing in its place: the story begins with God bringing order.

feedbackWrong.a: The darkness does not vanish; it remains, named Night. God sets it apart from the light.
feedbackWrong.b: The light is not hidden; it is put in its place, alongside the darkness.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-01-.hint: It is the action that puts each thing in its place.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-01-.question: What links Genesis 1:1 to Revelation 22:13?
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-01-.learningObjective: Relate the beginning of the Bible to its end.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-01-.feedbackCorrect: The Bible opens with "No princípio" and closes with "the Beginning and the End": all God's story.

feedbackWrong.a: Revelation speaks of a beginning and an end: "the Beginning and the End".
feedbackWrong.b: The end does not undo the beginning; the same Lord is in both.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-01-.hint: Look for the same word in both texts.

options.c: The one who begins the story also completes it

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-01-.question: Genesis 1:1 shows that the Bible's story begins with God, not with human beings.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-01-.learningObjective: Read the Bible as a story with God at the center from the very start.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-01-.feedbackCorrect: The Bible's first subject is God; human beings come in later, within his work.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread Genesis 1:1: before any person, "No princípio, Deus criou".

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-01-.hint: See who acts in the first sentence.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-01-.question: In Genesis 1:4, tap the phrase that shows the world begins approved by God.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-01-.learningObjective: Support from the text that creation begins good.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-01-.feedbackCorrect: God looks at what he made and approves: the story begins with a good world, not a broken one.

feedbackWrong.a: "Das trevas" tells what the light was separated from, not God's approval.
feedbackWrong.b: Separating shows order; the approval is in what God saw.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-01-.hint: Look for what God thought of what he made.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-01-.question: What reading does Genesis 1:1–2 support about this passage's place in the Bible?
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-01-.learningObjective: Choose the reading that places Genesis 1 as the beginning of the biblical story.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-01-.feedbackCorrect: Everything that follows happens in the world God created here: it is the story's first step.

feedbackWrong.b: The first subject is God: "No princípio, Deus criou".
feedbackWrong.c: The emptiness and darkness are the starting point; God sees that what he makes is good (Gen 1:4).
feedbackWrong.d: The God who creates here is the same one who, at the end of the Bible, makes all things new.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-01-.hint: Compare each option with who acts and with what comes next.

options.a: It is the start of the story the whole Bible tells
options.b: It is the start of humanity's story, not God's
options.c: It shows a world already born spoiled by evil
options.d: It is a stand-alone introduction, unconnected to the rest

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-01-.question: Which sequence shows the thread of creation that begins in Genesis 1:1?
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-01-.learningObjective: See Genesis 1:1 as the start of a thread that runs through the Bible to the end.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-01-.feedbackCorrect: The Bible moves from creation to the promise of a new creation, and ends with it in sight.

feedbackWrong.default: Follow the story: creation (Gen 1:1), promise (Isa 65:17), and fulfillment (Rev 21:1).

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-01-.hint: Follow the order of the Bible: Genesis, the prophets, Revelation.

options.a: God creates the heavens and the earth
options.b: God promises to create new heavens and a new earth
options.c: John sees a new heaven and a new earth

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-01-.question: In Genesis 1:1, what word marks the beginning of the whole biblical story?
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-01-.learningObjective: Remember the term that opens the biblical story.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-01-.feedbackCorrect: Before anything begins, God is already there: the Bible's story starts from him.

feedbackWrong.a: The text does not speak of silence; it speaks of the beginning of everything.
feedbackWrong.c: The heavens are what God created, not the time when everything begins.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-01-.hint: It is the word that tells when everything began.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-01-.question: What links Genesis 1:3 to 2 Corinthians 4:6?
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-01-.learningObjective: See how the NT rereads the light of creation in the work of Christ.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-01-.feedbackCorrect: Paul recalls Genesis: the God who made light at the start makes Christ's light shine in us.

feedbackWrong.b: Paul says "in our hearts": the light is for those who believe.
feedbackWrong.c: Paul speaks of the light that gives the knowledge of God's glory in Christ.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-01-.hint: See what Paul quotes from Genesis and where that light shines now.

options.a: God lights a light in the heart

estudo:entrada-biblia-01.context: The Bible brings together many books, written over centuries, but it tells a single story. It does not begin with a hero, a people, or a king. These first verses set the stage where everything that follows will happen.
estudo:entrada-biblia-01.focusQuestion: What difference does it make to read your life within a story that begins in God?
estudo:entrada-biblia-01.keywordGloss: The beginning of everything; the Bible opens its story with God already present and at work.
facts: The Bible begins with God creating the heavens and the earth.
Before the light, there was darkness over the face of the deep.
God speaks, and light comes into being.
God sees that the light is good and separates it from the darkness.
God names the light and the darkness: Day and Night.
The text marks evening and morning and counts the first day.
